learningMore.message: Learning reads only the recipients of your sent mail, never uses AI, and never overrides a block you set by hand. It works whether protection is on or off.

sentFoldersHint.message: These folders are watched for new sent mail, also mail sent from a phone or from webmail, and are read by the scan.

incomingHint.message: While protection is on, new mail in monitored folders is checked when it arrives, when Thunderbird starts and every 5 minutes. The check every 5 minutes is there because of other devices: Thunderbird does not report mail as new once you have read it on your phone, and mail you send from your phone teaches the white list the same way. It reads only what Thunderbird has already fetched.

monitoredHint.message: The Inbox of every account is always monitored. Add folders that receive new mail directly, for example through a server‑side rule.

aiSecretsHint.message: API keys and sign‑ins are stored unencrypted in your Thunderbird profile. They are never written to the log and never exported.

chatgptWelcomeText.message: Scoring mail from unknown senders, those on neither list, in Block Spam now uses your ChatGPT plan. You can review and manage the usage in ChatGPT settings.

signInWaiting.message: Sign in on the tab that opened. This page updates by itself when the sign‑in is complete.

signInManual.message: Sign in on the tab that opened, or in your browser. At the end the browser shows an error page for an address that starts with http://127.0.0.1:1455. That is expected: copy that address from the address bar, paste it into the field below, then press “Finish sign‑in” next to it.

signInPasteHint.message: If this page does not update by itself: at the end of the sign‑in the browser shows an error page for an address that starts with http://127.0.0.1:1455. That is expected. Copy that address from the address bar, paste it into the field below, then press “Finish sign‑in” next to it.

signInNoneInProgress.message: No sign‑in is in progress. Start again.

signInTimedOut.message: The sign‑in took too long and was cancelled.

signInError_state_mismatch.message: The address belongs to a different sign‑in attempt.

signInError_wrong_address.message: This is not the address the sign‑in redirects to. It starts with http://127.0.0.1:1455/auth/callback.

signInError_denied.message: Access was declined on the OpenAI page.

signInError_no_code.message: The address holds no sign‑in code. Copy the whole address from the address bar.

signInError_registration_incomplete.message: OpenAI did not register Block Spam for the sign‑in. Start the sign‑in again.

signInError_client_mismatch.message: The sign‑in answered for a different app than the one that started it. Start the sign‑in again.

signInError_exchange_failed.message: OpenAI did not complete the sign‑in: $1

signInError_invalid_token.message: The answer of OpenAI to the sign‑in is not valid: $1

signInError_account_mismatch.message: A different ChatGPT account signed in. Sign in with the account of this service, or add a new service.

signInError_plan_not_enabled.message: Permission to use your ChatGPT plan was not granted, so the service cannot be used. Start the sign‑in again and allow plan use.

shortcutsHint.message: The shortcuts act on the selected messages, or on the message shown in a tab or window. Block moves the messages to the Spam folder. Trust moves them back to the Inbox from the Spam folder or from a screening folder.

shortcutsMore.message: Your own messages are ignored. Blocking and trusting by hand work in observation mode and while protection is off. After a shortcut or the context menu, a desktop notification says what was done, and the panel of the Block Spam button in the toolbar lets you undo it.

shortcutsRebindHint.message: Opens Thunderbird’s own list of shortcuts. You also find it under Add‑ons and Themes: click the gear button (“Tools for all add‑ons”) and choose “Manage Extension Shortcuts”.

smartLabel.message: Smart: use the address for senders at public mail providers

smartHint.message: With Smart on, the domain commands (shortcuts, the “Whole domain” buttons of the panel and the context menu) block or trust a company as a whole domain and a sender at a provider such as gmail.com by address. With Smart off they always use the domain.

otherWaysTitle.message: Toolbar button, context menu and log

otherWaysPopup.message: Select one or more messages and click the Block Spam button in the toolbar. The panel says what the lists hold about the sender, offers buttons to block and to trust, and lets you undo the last command.

otherWaysMenu.message: Right‑click a message in the message list and choose Block Spam.

otherWaysLog.message: A decision can be undone with the button in its row.

bareKeysHint.message: Unfortunately a key on its own, such as B, cannot be a shortcut: Thunderbird lets an add‑on capture keys pressed without Alt, Ctrl or a similar key only if the add‑on is given full access to Thunderbird and your computer. Block Spam never asks for that.

publicHint.message: At a public provider such as gmail.com every address is a different person, so the lists hold single addresses there. For any other domain the whole company is trusted or blocked as one domain.

publicMore.message: The built‑in list has $1 providers. Changing it affects future entries only.

publicDomainName.message: Domain of a mail provider or of a company

publicInvalid.message: Enter a domain such as example.com.

publicIsPublic.message: $1 is treated as a public provider: entries are made per address.

publicIsCustom.message: $1 is treated as a company domain: entries are made for the whole domain.

publicRemovedTitle.message: Treated as company domains by you

forwardingHint.message: Some mailboxes forward mail to you in their own name, so the message shows the forwarding mailbox as its sender. Add them here: their messages are then judged by the original sender.

forwardingHowTo.message: How to tell: if a forwarded message shows the original author as its sender, nothing needs to be configured. If it shows the mailbox that forwarded it, add that mailbox here once.

forwardingMore.message: The trust of a forwarding mailbox is never passed on: a message whose original sender cannot be found counts as mail from an unknown sender, one on neither list.

forwardLabelsHint.message: When the original sender is not in the message headers, it is read from the first line of the text that starts with one of these labels. Separate the labels with commas.

forwardLabelsMore.message: Only after that is an attached message looked at. Add the label your forwarding mailbox writes before the original sender.

forwardLabelsUnused.message: The labels are not used yet: no forwarding mailbox is listed.

exportHint.message: One file with the lists, the settings and the AI services, without their keys and sign‑ins. Entries and folders of an account are saved with the account’s email address.

exportDone.message: The file was handed to Thunderbird for saving.

exportSkipped.message: Exported. Items of accounts that no longer exist were left out: $1.

importHint.message: “Merge lists” adds the entries of the file to your lists. An entry that is on the other list here moves to the list the file names. Settings and AI services stay untouched. “Replace everything” overwrites lists, settings and AI services.

importMore.message: After “Replace everything”, keys must be entered again and the ChatGPT sign‑in repeated. Importing never switches protection on. Items that belong to an account follow the account with the same email address here. The others are skipped and reported.

importNotJson.message: This file is not a Block Spam export.

importReplaceTitle.message: Replace lists, settings and AI services?

importReplaceText.message: Your current lists, settings and AI services are replaced by the file. Keys and sign‑ins are removed from this computer. This cannot be undone.

importEntries.message: Entries added: $1. Moved from the other list: $2. Already there: $3.

importMovedWhiteMore.message: Moved to the white list: $1 and $2 more.

importMovedBlackMore.message: Moved to the black list: $1 and $2 more.

importReplaced.message: The settings were replaced. AI services imported: $1. Enter their keys again.

importServicesOff.message: AI services imported switched off: $1. Your sent mail is not scanned yet, so they would get mail from people you already write to. Scan it first, then switch them on under $2.

importNoVerdictKept.message: Mail without an AI verdict still stays where it is. Your sent mail is not scanned yet, so mail from people you already write to would be moved. Scan it first, then choose again under $1.

importSkippedAccount.message: Skipped $1: no account with the address $2.

importSkippedFolder.message: Skipped the folder $1: it does not exist here.

importUndone.message: Import taken back. Entries removed again: $1. Entries moved back to the list they were on: $2.

popupDataProblemText.message: Block Spam could not read its stored data. Protection is off until this is resolved in the settings.

popupSetupText.message: Scan your sent mail first, so that mail from people you write to is never blocked or sent to an AI service.

popupSetupScanning.message: Your sent mail is being scanned. You can follow the scan in the settings.

popupSetupWaiting.message: Your sent mail is being scanned. Protection switches on when the scan has finished.

popupNoSelection.message: Select a message to block or trust its sender here.

popupDecisionLabel.message: $1, $2. Decision about this message: show in the log.

popupNoChange.message: Nothing to change: the sender is on this list already.

tipMoveJunk.message: Moves the message to the Spam folder.

tipMoveInbox.message: Moves the message back to the Inbox.

tipKeptBlack.message: The entry $1 stays on the black list.

tipKeptWhite.message: The entry $1 stays on the white list.

popupDomainDeciding.message: Whole domain $1, the entry that decided:

popupPublicNote.message: This is a public mail provider, so only this address is blocked or trusted.

popupOwnAddress.message: This is one of your own addresses.

popupUnknownSender.message: The original sender is not known. Blocking or trusting moves the message, but adds no entry.

popupScoreSelectedTitle.message: Sends the selected messages to your AI services and writes the scores to the log. Nothing is moved.

popupScoreConfirm.message: Selected messages: $1. Their content will be sent to your AI services, also for senders on your lists. Nothing is moved and no entry is created. The scores appear in the log.

popupScoreTooMany.message: Select at most $1 messages to score them in one run.

popupScoreDone.message: Scored: $1. The scores are in the log.

popupScoreDoneFailed.message: Scored: $1. Without a score: $2. The scores and the reasons are in the log.

popupScoreNone_one.message: No AI service answered: the message got no score. The log says why.

popupScoreNone_few.message: No AI service answered: none of the $1 messages got a score. The log says why.

popupScoreNone_many.message: No AI service answered: none of the $1 messages got a score. The log says why.

popupNothingSelected.message: Select one or more messages in the message list first.

notifyUnknownSender.message: Forwarded messages whose original sender is not known: $1. No entry was added for them.

notifyMoveFailed.message: Some messages could not be moved: $1

notifyNoInbox.message: The account has no Inbox folder

notifyUndoHint.message: To undo, click the Block Spam button in the toolbar.

commandUndone.message: Taken back. The lists are as they were before.

commandUndoneMany.message: Taken back: $1 entries. The lists are as they were before.

commandUndoNotFound.message: No longer found, so not moved back: $1

tooltip_observing.message: Block Spam: protection is on, observing only

tooltip_waiting.message: Block Spam: protection switches on after the scan

tooltip_invalid.message: Block Spam: stored data is not valid
